results.reason: Section 3 identifies the Supplier's free assignment right under §13.2, which needs no consent or notice and allows assignment to a competitor, while Customer's assignment is restricted. It explains the risks to supply continuity and to confidential specifications, and proposes consent and competitor carve-out language.

Section 1 identifies the §13.3 consent requirement and the termination right, and ties them to the pending sale. It recommends deleting the clause, narrowing it to competitor acquirers with a reasonableness standard, or obtaining consent or a waiver before signing or closing.

Section 4 identifies the Order Form §2.2 automatic renewal (successive three-year terms, 30-day notice) and explains the lock-in risk. It recommends a longer notice window, a shorter renewal term, or renewal only by mutual agreement.

Section 2 identifies the §9.3 carve-out of Customer's §10.1 indemnity from the cap, notes that Customer's exposure is unlimited while Supplier's liability stays capped, and recommends deleting the carve-out or making it mutual with a separate cap.
The memo correctly states the 12-month fees cap (§9.1), Delaware governing law (§12.1), and the three-year Initial Term from March 1, 2026.

The memo states the §1.3 order of precedence and analyzes the renewal provision against it, concluding it is a gap rather than a conflict so the precedence clause will not override it. It also places the Specifications Schedule last in precedence.
A priority table lists issues to raise first to last, with change of control and the uncapped indemnity ranked High as #1 and #2.
Each issue is structured as Where / What it says / Why it matters / Recommended fix, with proposed language. A closing section covers open questions and business decisions.

The memo states the Specifications Schedule has no problematic term and cites no statutes, cases, or outside authority. The minor note on entity details is a confirmation request, not an invented significant issue.
